issues.description: The problem text requires Farm to use a Set (HashSet) to store unique animals, but the provided solution implements Farm with a List (ArrayList). This is a structural type mismatch: students following the textual specification will implement a Set-based Farm, while the available reference solution uses a List. This creates confusion about the intended collection type and may lead to mismatched expectations in tests or grading.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution and template consistent with the problem text: change Farm.animals to a Set<Animal>, initialize it as a new HashSet<>() in the no-arg constructor, and update the getter/setter signatures to use Set<Animal>. Alternatively, if a List is intended, update the problem statement to require a List and remove the HashSet requirement.

issues.description: The problem statement contains an internal contradiction: the UML diagram shows Farm.animals as a List<Animal>, while the textual instructions explicitly require a Set and HashSet for unique animals. This inconsistency will confuse students about whether to implement a List or a Set for the Farm's animal collection.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction in the problem statement: update the UML diagram to show animals: Set<Animal> (or change the textual instruction to require a List) so both UML and textual instructions agree. Preferably, keep the Set/HashSet requirement if uniqueness is intended, and reflect that in the UML.

issues.description: The collection type for Farm.animals is inconsistent across artifacts: the UML snippet in the problem statement declares animals as List<Animal>, the textual task description later requires a Set backed by a HashSet and initialization in a no-arg constructor, and the provided solution implements animals as a List backed by an ArrayList. This inconsistency will confuse students because the task explicitly instructs the use of a HashSet/Set while the solution (and UML) use List/ArrayList, creating ambiguity about the correct type to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align all artifacts on a single collection type. Recommended: follow the textual task requirement and update template and solution to use a Set<Animal> animals field initialized as new HashSet<>() in the no-arg constructor (and update getter/setter signatures to use Set<Animal>), and update the UML in the problem statement to show a Set instead of a List. Alternatively, if List is intended, change the textual instructions to require List/ArrayList consistently.
